slice.target: Cargo vendored dependency integrity metadata suitable for ordinary repository-file transport
slice.action: One official Cargo documentation lookup for vendored-source integrity metadata.
slice.finding: Cargo's official Source Replacement documentation states that directory sources are suitable for checking vendored dependency source into source control and that each crate has an associated .cargo-checksum.json metadata file protecting against accidental modifications. Official Cargo API documentation further describes .cargo-checksum.json as containing SHA-256 checksums for package/source files and requires the checksum file beside Cargo.toml for directory sources created by cargo vendor.
slice.verified_scope: Vendored Cargo directory-source artifacts have documented per-crate integrity metadata in ordinary files, and the vendored source tree is designed to be suitable for source-control transport.
slice.not_verified_scope: The checksum metadata is not documented as a malicious-tamper security mechanism; this slice did not execute cargo vendor or Cargo, did not verify Chat-native process execution, and did not establish end-to-end richer-mode parity.

scope_guard: Treat this as source-qualified partial evidence for repository-file artifact transport and accidental-modification detection only, not Phase-1 acceptance of Cargo execution parity.
exact_continuation: On the next invocation, fresh-bootstrap and resume from this checkpoint. Audit exactly one official Cargo source for whether a pre-existing vendored directory source can be consumed fully offline after repository checkout with no registry/network access, while preserving the distinction between transporting prebuilt vendored artifacts and executing Cargo. Persist the exact result or blocker with zero-cost/quota classification and readback.
